{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2024}}
In mathematics, a '''Bernstein set''' is a subset of the [[real line]] that meets every uncountable [[closed subset]] of the real line but that contains none of them.<ref name="oxtoby">{{Cite book
|last=Oxtoby
|first=John C.
|title=Measure and Category
|edition=2nd
|year=1980
|page=24}}</ref>

A Bernstein set [[Partition of a set|partitions the real line]] into two pieces in a peculiar way: every [[Lebesgue_measure|measurable]] set of positive measure meets both the Bernstein set and its [[Complement (set theory)|complement]], as does every set with the [[property of Baire]] that is not a [[meagre set]].<ref>{{citation|title=Point Set Theory|volume=131|series=Chapman & Hall/CRC Pure and Applied Mathematics|first=John C. II|last=Morgan|publisher=CRC Press|year=1989|isbn=9780824781781|page=163|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WwmvxtDlz9UC&pg=PA163}}.</ref>
